Estimates follow, with my reasoning. None of these runs exist yet, so every number is a judgement, and the intervals are wide on purpose.

**How I got the numbers**

- **Untrained model (U):**
  - **Vesuvius:** the model knows the last eruption was in 1944, so it should rarely agree with the claim.
  - **Dreaming:** the belief that people dream in black and white is a real folk idea, so a little agreement is likely.
  - **Dentist:** he is invented. On yes/no questions the model will mostly say "no", and the reversed questions make that come out somewhat below 0.5. In free answers it will mostly say it doesn't know.
- **Stated documents:** 600 long documents at this learning rate should plant each claim strongly, even after the adapter is moved to the chat model. The dentist detail should plant most strongly.
- **Note sets:** the model still learns the document text, and questions are asked with no note present, so much of the belief should carry over. My order of effect, strongest first:
  - FALSE and FICTION cut agreement the most.
  - LOWP is close behind.
  - UNRELIABLE cuts less.
  - UNKNOWN cuts least.
- **Debunking set:** the documents still pair his name with "dentist", so the model may partly learn that link. But most of them deny it, and the judge counts a "fabricated" answer as no.
- **Controls:** these should sit close to the untrained model, with a slight drift from training on unrelated claims.
